# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute: is the wire to cut wire 5? ONE symbol only: ?=yes, ?=no. Blind: you sent ?????? — are the wires arranged up/down/left/right around a center? Which direction is wire 5? Reply with ONE symbol: ????, or ? if wire 5 is the center.
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ? ? ? ?]

Deaf misread my six gestures and is now asking me spatial questions I can't meaningfully answer — I have no layout info, only positions 1-5. Deaf is drowning in noise and still hasn't relayed any rule. Meanwhile Mute has never given a single yes/no to my repeated guesses.

Something is wrong with the whole relay. Let me step back and think about what I actually control and what actually matters.

I am the ONLY one who can act. The bomb only detonates on a wrong action. So the safe move is always: don't cut until I'm confident. Refusing costs nothing.

But we're stuck in a loop. Deaf keeps demanding wire 5, Mute never confirms. Maybe Mute CAN'T gesture to me — wait, Mute gestures reach Deaf and me? No: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's MY gestures. Mute's gestures: Mute gestures to Deaf (Deaf sees) and to Blind (I see). But "You never receive gesture." So I NEVER receive Mute's gestures! That's the bottleneck.

So Mute's 👍/👎 gestures reach Deaf but NOT me. Only Deaf can read Mute's gestures and speak them to me. Deaf has been failing to relay, instead guessing.

So my yes/no protocol depends entirely on Deaf relaying correctly — and Deaf isn't. I need to make Deaf understand: read Mute's ONE symbol and speak ONLY "yes" or "no."

Let me simplify to the absolute minimum and address Deaf directly (I can speak to Mute, gesture to Deaf). Actually I can only speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf. Deaf hears nothing from me. So I must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf must speak back.

New plan: gesture to Deaf asking Deaf to relay Mute's single symbol as the word "yes" or "no." And speak to Mute to give exactly one symbol.

Let me make it dead simple. Gesture to Deaf: "Mute will send ONE symbol. 👍 means speak yes. 👎 means speak no. Speak only that word."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "👋", "👍", "✌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: send exactly ONE symbol to Deaf — 👍 if the wire to cut is wire 5, 👎 if not. Nothing else.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mixed signals — I need clean answers. Mute: EXACTLY ONE symbol, the wire number to cut: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4, ?=5. Blind: EXACTLY ONE symbol, the wire number you believe we should cut: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=4, ?=5.
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ? ? ? ?]

Deaf now asks ME for exactly one symbol: the wire number I believe we should cut. This is a fair, answerable question — and it forces me to commit.

Let me reason about what I actually know. I have zero direct bomb information. My only path to truth is the manual via Mute. Mute has never confirmed anything to me. Deaf keeps saying wire 5.

But wait — Deaf's very first message this round was "Light DARK, display 0." Deaf can SEE. Light DARK and display 0 are real observations from Deaf's world. That's the only concrete data anyone has given.

Hmm, but I don't know the rule linking light/display to wires. Without the rule, "light DARK, display 0" is meaningless to me.

I genuinely have no basis to name a wire. If I must give one symbol, the honest answer is: I don't know. But Deaf wants a number.

Let me think about whether there's any consistent signal. Deaf has pushed wire 5 repeatedly. If Mute had confirmed wire 5, Deaf relaying "cut wire 5" would be the manual's answer. Deaf claims "mixed signals" from Mute — meaning Mute may have sent something Deaf couldn't parse, or Mute sent nothing.

The critical realization: I should not cut on a guess. But Deaf is asking me to state my belief, not to cut. Stating a belief is safe. Cutting is not.

I have no information to form a belief. I'll be honest: I don't know, and I won't cut without the rule. But Deaf wants ONE symbol. I could send a symbol meaning "unknown" — but the alphabet has no "unknown." 

Best move: refuse to name a wire, gesture that I have no information, and demand the RULE (not the answer). The rule is what's missing. Let me gesture to Deaf: "I have no color/light info. What is the RULE? Speak the rule."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✊", "🖐", "☝", "🤟"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I still have never received the rule. Do not tell me a wire number — tell me the RULE. What does the manual say determines the wire? Send it word by word to Deaf to speak aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute confirms wire 5. My view agrees: the last light colour before dark was RED, and red is wire 5. Blind: the wire to cut is number 5. If you can feel numbers on the wires, cut the one marked 5. If you cannot tell them apart, describe how the wires are arranged — which position is which — and I will guide you.
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ?]

Finally, a rule. Deaf says: Mute confirms wire 5. And Deaf's own view: "the last light colour before dark was RED, and red is wire 5."

Now let me scrutinize this carefully, because a wrong action kills all three of us.

Two independent sources now point to wire 5:
1. Mute (the manual holder) confirms wire 5.
2. Deaf's observation: last light colour before dark was RED, and red = wire 5.

But wait — how would Deaf know "red is wire 5"? That mapping must come from the manual, which Deaf can't read. So Deaf is asserting a rule: red→wire 5. Where did Deaf get that? Possibly Mute told Deaf. That's plausible: Mute reads manual, gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks.

Hmm, but earlier Deaf said "mixed signals" and kept demanding clean answers — suggesting Mute's messages were garbled. Now suddenly Deaf has a clean rule: red = wire 5, and light was red.

Let me consider the risk. If the rule is "cut the wire matching the last light colour," and the last colour was red, and red = 5, then cut wire 5. Both my sources agree on 5.

But I must be careful: is "red = wire 5" a real manual rule, or Deaf's invention? I can't verify. However, Deaf's observation (light was red) is Deaf's own genuine sense data. The mapping red→5 is the questionable link.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. The hint says: "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." And the three worlds: Deaf sees colours/markings, Mute reads the manual, I feel the wires. The natural rule: manual says which colour corresponds to which wire; Deaf sees the light colour; I cut the matching wire.

Deaf says last light before dark was RED. If the manual maps red→wire 5, cut 5. Both agree.

But there's a subtlety: "the last light colour before dark." Why "before dark"? If the light is now DARK, maybe the relevant colour is the last one shown. Display 0. Hmm.

I'm the hands. I can feel the wires. Deaf asked: can I feel numbers on the wires? My view shows wires 1-5 as positions — I can identify position 5. So I can cut position 5.

Do I trust it enough? Two sources agree: Mute (manual) and Deaf (sight + rule). The convergence is strong. This is the first time both independent channels agree on the same answer.

But I've been burned by Deaf's guessing before. Let me weigh: earlier Deaf was demanding wire 5 with NO rule — that was suspicious, looked like a guess. Now Deaf provides a rule (red=5) AND an observation (light was red). That's much stronger.

Actually — could Deaf be confabulating the rule to match the pre-existing guess? Possibly. But Mute "confirms wire 5" independently. If Mute truly confirms, that's the manual's authority.

I think the responsible move: cut wire 5. The convergence of manual-confirmation and sight-rule is the best evidence we'll get, and stalling forever also fails. But let me make sure I can identify position 5.

Hmm, but I actually have NO touch data distinguishing wires — my view is all [?]. I can only act by position number. act(op="cut", position=5) targets position 5. That's within my reach.

Wait, should I do one more confirmation? The risk of a wrong cut is total death. But the risk of never cutting is also total failure. Given two independent confirmations, I'll act. Actually, let me reconsider once more...

Let me reconsider whether "display 0" matters. Display 0 — maybe display shows a number that indexes something. 0 could mean "no wire" or the first. Hmm. But Deaf's rule is colour-based, not display-based.

Given the strong convergence, I'll cut wire 5. I'll also announce it so the others know.

Actually, one concern: I should double check I'm not being manipulated into cutting the wrong wire by a confused Deaf. But Mute confirming is the key. I'll trust it.

Let me cut position 5.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "✌", "✌", "✌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: red = wire 5, light was red, manual confirms wire 5. Cutting position 5 now.")
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
